title: Mount project NAS and enable workbench HDF5 upload
goal: Mount the project NAS NFS export at /mnt/nas on this workstation, then enable the existing Robot Capture HDF5 upload path to /mnt/nas/forge/franka/raw without changing capture, recording, or upload code semantics.
doneWhen: An absent NAS fails closed instead of being replaced by a local directory write
/mnt/nas/forge/franka/raw is writable by the workbench user and a probe file round-trips
config/workbench.yaml upload is enabled with transport=local, remote_raw_dir=/mnt/nas/forge/franka/raw, robot_name=franka-pico
Upload sink probe and offline upload tests pass; remaining unvalidated items are reported
decisions: Mount uses systemd automount + _netdev + nofail so boot never blocks and access to an absent NAS fails instead of writing into an empty local /mnt/nas
Soft NFS timeouts preferred over hard so the long-running workbench cannot wedge in uninterruptible IO; upload already verifies remote size after transfer and retries
Only workbench upload configuration changes; app/upload.py, sink_health.py, recorder and capture code stay untouched
Forge-side franka adapter support is out of scope for this task

verification.summary: NAS is mounted persistently and the workbench uploads real recordings to /mnt/nas/forge/franka/raw.
checks: /mnt/nas mounted from 192.168.10.35:/volume1/robo-data-warehouse, persisted in /etc/fstab (vers=3, hard, _netdev, nofail); this host is now 192.168.10.38 and is present in the NAS export allow-list
write probe as embody under /mnt/nas/forge/franka/raw passed
probe_sink with the active config returns ok
201 of 238 local sessions reported upload_status=uploaded; NAS holds 18G across left_arm_pick_cube (101) and pick_green_cube (100)
limitations: Operator installed the mount with hard NFS timeouts, not the soft variant in scripts/setup_nas_mount.sh; a NAS outage during a transfer can wedge the writing process
Robot Forge has no confirmed franka adapter; converted LeRobot output for these recordings does not exist yet
The workbench was not running at completion time
